title: Commutation of noise and low degree projection
statement: Let $P$ be a product of $n$ finite probability spaces with strictly positive atom masses, and let $\Omega=\prod_{i=0}^{n-1}\Omega_i$ be its outcome space. For every real $\rho$, every $k\in\mathbb N$, and every function $f:\Omega\to\mathbb R$, applying the noise operator with parameter $\rho$ to the low degree projection of $f$ gives the same function as taking the low degree projection of the noise operator applied to $f$.
hypotheses_covered: $P$ is a product of $n$ finite probability spaces
Every atom mass is strictly positive and each coordinate's masses sum to one
replaced: Let $P$ be a product of $n$ finite probability spaces with strictly positive atom masses and outcome space $\Omega=\prod_i\Omega_i$, $\rho\in\mathbb R$, $k\in\mathbb N$, and $f:\Omega\to\mathbb R$. Then $T_\rho(f^{\le k})=(T_\rho f)^{\le k}$.
